shorts.title: What you will learn: Comparison and logical operators
shorts.hook: Every decision in your program starts as true or false.
shorts.script: Every decision in your program starts as true or false. Today we ask questions in code. Is a number bigger? Are two values equal? Each answer is true or false. A comparison asks a question about two values. The answer is a bool, so it is true or false. The comparison operators are less than, greater than, equal to and not equal to. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.caption: What you will learn: Comparison and logical operators.

shorts.title: Comparison and logical operators in one minute
shorts.hook: A comparison asks a question about two values.
shorts.script: A comparison asks a question about two values. The answer is a bool, so it is true or false. The comparison operators are less than, greater than, equal to and not equal to. The logical operators join tests. And needs both tests to be true. Or needs only one. Not flips the answer. Think of a cinema gate. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.caption: Comparison and logical operators in one minute.

shorts.title: Inside the second program
shorts.script: The mark is seventy-two. A valid mark must be at least zero and at most one hundred. We join two tests with and. A pass needs at least thirty-five. Both bools print as true. Always write the two tests in full. Never write zero less than mark less than one hundred. The program prints true and true. A comparison gives a bool. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.caption: Inside the second program.

shorts.title: Bug of the Day: One equals sign instead of two
shorts.hook: Can you spot the bug in comparison and logical operators?
shorts.script: Can you spot the bug in comparison and logical operators? Bug of the Day. Here the if test uses one equals sign. That does not compare. It stores zero in seats. The compiler warns about an assignment used as a truth value. Use two equals signs to compare. Always read warnings. They often point at real bugs. A single equals sign stores a value. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.caption: Bug of the Day: One equals sign instead of two.

shorts.title: Pun and challenge
shorts.hook: Can you test whether a year is a leap year
shorts.script: Can you test whether a year is a leap year in comparison and logical operators? Why was the boolean so honest? It only knew true or false. Write one bool expression that is true when a number is even and bigger than ten. Write your answer in the comments. A comparison gives a bool. Use two equals signs to test for equality. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
